plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers on sturdy stems above blue-green strap-like leaves. Thousands of cultivars exist, ranging from single early types to frilled parrot and double forms. It is a hallmark of spring gardens in temperate climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; famous displays in the Netherlands, such as Keukenhof, and in temperate gardens in North America and Europe
plants.funFact: In the 1630s, tulip bulbs in the Netherlands became so valuable during 'Tulip Mania' that a single rare bulb could cost more than a house.

plants.name: Hyacinthoides non-scripta
plants.description: A woodland bulb that forms dense carpets beneath deciduous trees, with drooping, one-sided spikes of fragrant, bell-shaped flowers. It thrives in ancient, undisturbed woodlands and is an indicator of old forest habitat.
plants.location: Native to the British Isles, western France, Spain, and Belgium woodlands
plants.funFact: The UK holds roughly half of the world's bluebell population, and it is illegal to dig up wild bluebells there under the Wildlife and Countryside Act.

plants.name: Cornus florida
plants.description: A small deciduous understory tree whose showy 'flowers' are actually four large petal-like bracts surrounding a cluster of tiny greenish-yellow true flowers. Its horizontal branching gives it an elegant layered form, and it turns red in autumn with bright red fruits.
plants.location: Eastern North America, from southern Ontario to Florida and west to eastern Texas
plants.funFact: Flowering dogwood is the state tree of Virginia and North Carolina, and its hard wood was once used to make weaving shuttles and golf club heads.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A fast-growing, semi-deciduous tree with fern-like foliage and large panicles of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In the Northern Hemisphere tropics and subtropics it blooms in late spring, while in the Southern Hemisphere its main bloom is in October to November, although some trees flower in other seasons in warm regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics (May to June); October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); widely planted in Mexico, southern California, Florida, and the Mediterranean
plants.funFact: In Mexico City, jacaranda trees bloom around March to May, carpeting streets in purple, and the tree's flowers falling is said by some to be a sign of good luck.
